newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Senate raises farm spending in budget draft.
newsitem.headline: Polish Senate raises farm spending in budget draft.

text.p: The upper house of Poland's parliament, the Senate, passed late on Friday 14 amendments to the 1997 budget draft, increasing budget spending on agriculture and cutting budget reserves, PAP news agency said.
Senators voted 67 to 18 with three abstentions for the amended budget draft, which will now go back to the lower house, the Sejm, for a final vote before it is signed into law by the president.
Senators proposed to allot an extra 220 million zlotys for farming investment subsidies, higher credits for the purchase of agriculture products and for creating new jobs in rural areas.
The Senate said 59 million zlotys for that purpose would come from underestimated tax revenues, 60 million from underestimated duties and 100 million from underestimated personal income taxes.
The Senate also voted to decrease the budget reserve by spending 31 million on a wage rise as compensation for higher than planned inflation in 1996 and 20 million zlotys on building new schools.

The budget, with deficit set at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, envisages cutting year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December 1997, from 18.5 percent last year, while keeping economic growth at 5.5 percent.
